$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure App Services. One entry per console section; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py — a claim the backend does not honour fails CI. GCP/Azure probes aren't understood by the shared probe() helper (it speaks AWS wire), so every claim here is proven by `tests` instead.

azure.appservices.webapp.crud.title: Web Apps (create, list, get, delete, start/stop/restart)

azure.appservices.plan.crud.title: App Service plans (create, list, get, delete)
limitations: Capacity/worker metrics are not simulated; SKU is stored but does not change quota enforcement.

azure.appservices.webapp.config.title: Configuration (General settings: stack, platform, TLS, debugging, client certificates)
limitations: Settings are stored and returned to SDKs/az CLI; most (TLS version, FTP state, Always On, ...) are not enforced by a running workload.

azure.appservices.webapp.slots.title: Deployment slots (create, list, delete, swap)
limitations: Swap exchanges config/app settings/connection strings only; no real traffic routing or warm-up.

azure.appservices.webapp.customdomains.title: Custom domains (hostname bindings)
limitations: No real DNS/TXT ownership verification or TLS binding; the hostname is accepted and attached to the site.

azure.appservices.webapp.locks.title: Locks (resource-scoped management locks)
limitations: A CanNotDelete/ReadOnly lock on the Web App really blocks delete/write requests on it (409 ScopeLocked), but enforcement is scoped to the exact locked resource — it does not cascade from a resource-group- or subscription-scoped lock the way real ARM would.

azure.appservices.webapp.logs.title: App Service logs (application logging level, HTTP logs quota/retention)
limitations: Settings round-trip; there is no running workload to actually emit application/HTTP logs.

azure.appservices.webapp.activitylog.title: Activity log
limitations: Records create/update/delete/start/stop/restart/swap operations on the Web App and its sub-resources (slots, custom domains, locks, configuration); filters (severity, timespan, resource group) and export/columns actions are not simulated.

azure.appservices.webapp.iam.title: Access control (IAM): role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions). The Role assignments list is ENFORCED scoped to this Web App (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view) instead of the whole subscription — the same engine the Cosmos DB account and VM blades use; Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too).

Assignments are still created at the subscription scope (az role assignment create); 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation and Deny assignments / Classic administrators remain an honest gap. Update: the Deny assignments list, Classic administrators (a read-only list of the subscription's account administrator, like the real API) and My access (the simulated signed-in principal, evaluated with checkAccess) are now real shared tabs (azure.common.*); the gap wording above predates them.

azure.appservices.webapp.deploymentcente.title: Deployment Center (CI/CD source, FTPS credentials)
limitations: Real ARM control plane plus real deployments through the shared CI seam (core/ci_core.py): sourcecontrols/web (repo URL, branch, manual/continuous integration, GitHub Actions with a generated workflow YAML; scmType maintained), deployments + log, publishing credentials and basic-auth policies. Local Git (scmType LocalGit): a push (POST .../localgit, a Vyomi extension of the Kudu git receiver; with the Gitea git host (offline, VYOMI_CI_GITEA=1) a real git clone URL and real `git push`) commits to the app's repo, builds, and records a Success/Failed deployment with the build log. GitHub source: the branch tarball is fetched (public, or private with the user's own personal access token entered in the Deployment Center; stored server-side, never shown) and built on the offline appliance; on Nano there is no outbound HTTP so a GitHub sync is a Failed deployment saying so (Local Git works on Nano). Azure Repos / Bitbucket / generic git cannot be fetched (no HTTP git client) and are recorded Failed with that reason. The build produces a content-addressed package artifact (Dockerfile validated; container image builds use BuildKit on the offline appliance only); the App Service runtime does not hot-swap to the deployed package, the GitHub Actions workflow is generated and, when a personal access token is supplied (properties.vyomiAccessToken; offline appliance only - Nano cannot reach GitHub), committed to the connected repository through the GitHub Contents API (without a token it is generated but not committed; the pipeline itself runs on GitHub), and OAuth account authorization is not performed (PAT only).

azure.appservices.webapp.monitoring.title: Monitoring (Alerts, Metrics, Logs, Advisor recommendations, Health check, Diagnostic settings, Log stream, Process explorer)
limitations: Diagnostic settings (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings) are real: create/list/delete round-trip through the same generic engine every other Azure resource's Diagnostic settings page uses, scoped to this Web App's resource id. Export to the Log Analytics workspace is not simulated (no log/metric pipeline writes land there).
Alerts, Metrics, Logs, Advisor recommendations, Health check, Log stream and Process explorer have no metrics pipeline, alert evaluation or live log/process streaming behind them for Web Apps.

azure.appservices.webapp.devtools.title: Development Tools (Clone App, Console, Advanced Tools, App Service Editor, Extensions)
limitations: Clone App is real (azure.appservices.webapp.clone). Console, Advanced Tools, App Service Editor, Extensions, Process explorer and Log stream each have their own capability id (…console, …kudu, …appeditor, …extensions, …processes, …logstream) over the Kudu surface in core/azure_kudu_core.py; see those entries for what is real and what is limited.
api: sites/kudu/api (Vyomi extension mirroring the Kudu REST API)

azure.appservices.webapp.api.title: API (API Management link, API definition, CORS)
limitations: CORS allowed origins / credentials are stored on siteConfig.cors and returned to SDKs/az CLI; Vyomi has no real HTTP layer in front of the app, so the rule is never actually enforced against a cross-origin request.
No API Management linkage or OpenAPI/Swagger definition import.

azure.appservices.webapp.platform.title: Authentication, Identity, Application Insights, Backups, Certificates, Networking, WebJobs, Service Connector
limitations: Identity: enabling a system-assigned managed identity mints a stable principalId/tenantId that can be the subject of a role assignment on Access control (IAM); user-assigned identities are not modelled.

Backups: modelled as snapshots — backup configuration (storage URL, schedule) and on-demand/scheduled backup records (status, size, timestamp) round-trip for real, and Restore acknowledges, but there is no real site content to archive or replay.
Authentication providers, Application Insights linkage, TLS/SSL certificates, private endpoints, WebJobs and Service Connector are not modelled.

azure.appservices.webapp.scale.title: Scale up/out, Change App Service plan, Quotas
limitations: Scale up changes the plan's SKU, Scale out changes siteConfig.numberOfWorkers, and Change App Service plan re-points serverFarmId at another existing plan in the same resource group and OS — all real, round-tripping ARM PATCHes.
No capacity is actually added or removed: Vyomi does not run multiple instances, autoscale rules are not evaluated, and quota usage (Quotas page) is not tracked.

azure.appservices.webapp.automation.title: Automation (Tasks, Export template)
limitations: No Automation Tasks or ARM/Bicep/Terraform template export for the Web App.

azure.appservices.defender.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (this web app's recommendations)
limitations: Shows the live Defender for Cloud recommendations for this resource from Vyomi's rule engine (see azure.defender.recommendations); Azure's full built-in recommendation catalogue is not reproduced.

azure.appservices.webapp.support.title: Diagnose and solve problems, Events (preview), Resource visualizer, Resource health, New support request
limitations: No diagnostics engine, Event Grid wiring, resource visualizer, resource-health telemetry or support-ticket flow.

azure.appservices.webapp.siteconfigpanel.title: Default documents, Path mappings, Error pages, Health check, API definition, API Management link
limitations: Stored on the site configuration and returned by the API exactly as set; Vyomi runs no web server, so documents are not served, mappings/error pages/health probes are not applied and the API Management link imports nothing.

azure.appservices.webapp.webjobs.title: WebJobs (triggered and continuous)
limitations: Triggered Python scripts really execute in a restricted sandbox (no filesystem, network or subprocess); other runtimes are refused at run time.
Continuous jobs only track Running/Stopped; schedules (CRON) are stored, not fired.
Job definitions are created by ARM PUT (Vyomi addition); real Azure uploads them via Kudu.

azure.appservices.webapp.serviceconnecto.title: Service Connector
limitations: Creating a connection validates the target in this subscription and writes the real connection app settings (endpoint, plus a generated secret for secret auth); there is no network path, firewall rule or role assignment created for the target.

azure.appservices.webapp.quotas.title: Quotas
limitations: File system storage limit is the published figure per plan tier; usage counts only the content Vyomi stores for the app (function code, WebJob scripts). CPU, memory and bandwidth quotas are not reported.

azure.appservices.webapp.authentication.title: Authentication (App Service authentication)
limitations: Only the on/off platform switch and one shared bearer token exist (enforced on function invocation for function apps); identity providers and interactive sign-in are not simulated.

azure.appservices.webapp.autoscale.title: Autoscale
limitations: Stored as a Microsoft.Insights/autoscaleSettings resource on the plan; Vyomi runs no instances, so profiles and rules are never evaluated and the instance count does not change.

azure.appservices.webapp.certificates.title: Certificates
limitations: Uploaded PFX files are stored with a SHA-1 thumbprint of the file; Vyomi does not parse the certificate, so subject, issuer and expiry are not read from it.
Managed certificates are issued locally (not by a public CA) and are not trusted by anything.

azure.appservices.webapp.clone.title: Clone App
limitations: Copies the site configuration, app settings and connection strings into a new app; there is no site content to copy and slots, backups and custom domains are not cloned.

azure.appservices.webapp.networking.title: Networking: regional VNet integration, access restrictions, hybrid connections
limitations: Inbound access restrictions are ENFORCED on requests to a Function App site (offline: /azure-data/functions/{app}/{fn}): rules evaluated by ascending priority, first match wins, implicit Deny all once an Allow rule exists, vnet-subnet / service-tag / Front Door x-azure-fdid header rules matched against the caller identity declared with x-vyomi-source-ip / x-vyomi-source-subnet / x-vyomi-source-service-tag headers (an undeclared caller is an unknown public client). 403 Forbidden otherwise. Nano has no site front end, so there it is validated config only; web apps (non-function) have no served runtime in Vyomi to enforce against.

Regional VNet integration (create-time virtualNetworkSubnetId and networkConfig/virtualNetwork) checks the subnet exists, is delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms, is at least a /28, is in the app's region, is not used by another plan, and that the plan is Basic or higher; virtualNetworkConnections and vnetRouteAllEnabled follow. Access restrictions (main + SCM) validate priorities, actions, CIDRs, service tags, subnet service endpoints and Front Door header rules, and derive the implicit Allow all / Deny all rule and default action. Hybrid connections validate the relay ARM URI, endpoint, port and the per-plan limit (Basic 5, Standard 25, Premium 200) and stay NotConnected. No traffic flows through the VNet or relay and access restrictions are not enforced on inbound requests.

azure.appservices.applicationinsights.title: Application Insights (component, requests, failures, dependencies, events)
limitations: A real Microsoft.Insights/components resource linked through the app's connection string; requests / failures / dependencies / events / traces are read from the OTLP-ingested trace + log store (and requests Vyomi measured for the app). No Kusto query engine, Live Metrics stream or Application Map.

On Nano the telemetry recorder (OTLP spans, request counters, logs) lives in the open console page's memory: it is kept while the console stays open and starts empty after a page reload, whereas the offline appliance keeps it for the life of the appliance process.

azure.appservices.webapp.kudu.title: Advanced Tools (Kudu): environment, settings, deployments, tool links
limitations: Served as an ARM extension under sites/{site}/kudu/api (vfs, command, processes, deployments, settings, environment, logstream, siteextensions), not as a separate https://{site}.scm.azurewebsites.net host, so the real Kudu dashboard UI and its Git/zip-deploy endpoints are not served there (use Deployment Center / the Local Git extension).
Settings (SCM_*) are stored and read back; they do not change Kudu behaviour. Deployments are the Deployment Center records.

azure.appservices.webapp.console.title: Console (Kudu command console over the site's files and app settings)
limitations: There is no operating-system process behind the simulated site, so programs cannot be executed; the interpreter covers file, environment and process-listing commands only.

Supported: pwd cd ls cat echo head tail wc grep mkdir touch rm cp mv env printenv ps whoami hostname date uname tree find, pipes and > / >> redirection. Anything else returns 'command not found'. Writes are real edits to the site's file store; the running (sandboxed) function code is not hot-reloaded by them.

azure.appservices.webapp.appeditor.title: App Service Editor (edit the site's deployed files)
limitations: Edits the site's virtual file system (Deployment Center package contents, function sources, hostingstart.html, log files). Edits layer on top of deployed content and persist; the simulated runtime does not hot-swap to edited files. No syntax highlighting, no Git or debugging integration.

azure.appservices.webapp.processes.title: Process explorer (processes of the site's runtime)
limitations: The process table is MODELLED from the site's real state (runtime worker per instance, the Kudu/scm process, running continuous WebJobs); CPU time is the sum of the real measured invocation durations. It is not an operating-system process table: no kill/dump/profile actions and no per-thread detail.

azure.appservices.webapp.logstream.title: Log stream (live tail of the site's logs)
limitations: Tails real recorded lines (function invocations, WebJob runs, deployments, lifecycle and console actions) by polling a cursor every 2 seconds; stdout of a long-running workload does not exist because the simulated site runs no always-on process. Application logging level is reported but does not filter lines.

azure.appservices.webapp.extensions.title: Extensions (site extension gallery and install state)
limitations: Windows apps only (Linux apps return 400, as in Azure). The gallery is a bundled list of well-known extensions; install/uninstall records state and a marker file under /home/SiteExtensions — the extension's own code is not downloaded or executed.
